transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

My sleep has been all over the place for weeks, and I can’t seem to get any real rest no matter how exhausted I feel. I'm just so incredibly tired all the time, and I really need help figuring out how to get some actual sleep.

Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep at night, or is the main problem that your sleep schedule is shifted so you sleep at the wrong times, like being unable to sleep until very late and then sleeping during the day?

It’s definitely trouble falling and staying asleep at night, rather than a shifted daytime schedule. I lie awake for hours listening for my husband’s breathing and then jolt awake every hour to check his cardiac monitor. Even when I do manage to get some sleep, I wake up feeling like I've been hit by a truck instead of rested.
Have you had trouble sleeping for at least 3 nights a week over the past month, and is it causing problems with your daytime functioning?

Yes, it’s been happening almost every single night for well over a month now. It has severely impacted my days; I've been making careless errors with radiographs at the clinic, and I'm just too exhausted to handle basic household chores or even see my friends.
Is your sleep problem mainly happening because of anxiety, stress, pain, medications, or another medical issue, or does it seem to occur on its own without a clear cause?

It is heavily tied to the stress and anxiety of caring for my husband, since I'm constantly staying awake to listen to his breathing and check his cardiac monitor. However, I also have these periods where I feel incredibly wired and full of ideas, and I just don't feel the need for sleep at all, waking up after only a few hours. It really feels like a mix of both.

When you have those periods of feeling wired and needing very little sleep, do you also have other symptoms like unusually high energy, racing thoughts, increased talkativeness, impulsive spending, or feeling overly confident?

Yes, during those phases I feel this surge of energy and start talking a mile a minute, buzzing around to start multiple work and home projects at once. I also get quite impulsive, like driving much more aggressively and ordering expensive garden equipment and bird feeders online without even checking our budget.
During those energized periods, do you also feel unusually happy or irritable, have racing thoughts, or become more talkative than usual for at least a few days?

Yes, I felt oddly upbeat and wired, but also highly irritable and would snap at anyone who got in my way. I'd talk a mile a minute about new projects as if everything was incredibly urgent, and these spells would usually last for about a week.

During those week-long energized periods, did you ever have symptoms like needing much less sleep without feeling tired, racing thoughts, or doing things that caused serious problems at work, at home, or with money?

Yes, during those times I only slept three or four hours a night but woke up full of ideas and didn't feel tired at all. It caused serious issues, including formal write-ups at my clinic for imaging errors, strained relationships with my friends, and spending too much money online on expensive gardening and birding gear. I also drove way too fast and aggressively, which was really risky.
Have these energized, high-energy periods ever lasted at least 4 days in a row, and did they cause clear problems at work, at home, or with money?

Yes, those high-energy phases typically lasted about a week, where I'd barely sleep but still feel incredibly driven. They absolutely caused major problems, leading to impulsive online spending on expensive gear, aggressive driving, and contributing to the cycle that got me written up at work and strained my relationships.

Have you ever had a period of feeling so unusually energized or irritable that you needed hospitalization, became psychotic, or the symptoms were severe enough to make it impossible to function at all?

No, I've never been hospitalized or experienced anything like psychosis, and I was still able to function during those high phases. In fact, I actually felt unusually productive and was working constantly, even though it was quite chaotic and I was snapping at people.
Outside of those week-long energized periods, have you ever had times of feeling depressed, hopeless, or losing interest in things for at least two weeks?

Yes, absolutely, and they last much longer than two weeks; this current heavy, dark stretch has been hanging over me for close to a year now. I feel completely hollow and sad, and I've totally lost interest in things I used to love, like my Saturday birdwatching walks and tending to my garden.
Have your week-long energized periods ever happened without any major stress or sleep loss beforehand, and did they still occur even when you were otherwise feeling well?

I'm not really sure, as I haven't noticed them happening without some kind of stress. These highs and lows have mostly been occurring over the past year since my husband's health declined and my sleep became so disrupted.
Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt unusually energetic or irritable with much less need for sleep, even when you were not under major stress or sleep-deprived?

Yes, I had a period of about a week where I felt extremely wired, upbeat, and irritable, sleeping only three to four hours a night but waking up full of energy and not feeling tired at all. While these episodes have occurred during the stressful period of caring for my husband this past year, that feeling of having endless energy and not needing sleep was highly unusual and distinct from normal stress or exhaustion.

Have your high-energy periods ever lasted at least 4 days and caused a clear change in your behavior, even if you were still able to function, or are they only brief moments of feeling stressed and unable to sleep?

Yes, they definitely lasted about a week and represented a major, distinct shift in my behavior rather than just stress. During those times, I felt incredibly wired on only three or four hours of sleep, frantically taking on projects at work and home and making impulsive purchases. It was a complete contrast to my normal, structured self.
When you have those week-long high-energy periods, do you also notice racing thoughts, increased talkativeness, or feeling unusually confident or restless compared with your usual self?

Yes, I felt exactly like that during those weeks. I was talking a mile a minute about new projects because I felt unusually confident that all my ideas were urgent and brilliant. I also felt incredibly wired and restless, constantly buzzing around the clinic and my house trying to get things done.
Outside of your high-energy weeks, have you also had clear periods of depression or low mood lasting at least two weeks, or are the sleep problems mainly the only issue?

No, the sleep issues are definitely not the only problem, as I have been struggling with a deep, heavy low mood that has hung over me for close to a year now. It feels like someone turned the color down on my whole life, leaving me feeling hollow, incredibly sad, and constantly on the verge of tears.
During your low periods, do you also have symptoms like poor appetite or weight change, feeling worthless or guilty, trouble concentrating, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Yes, I often forget to eat and just survive on coffee because food tastes like cardboard, and I feel like a terrible vet tech and caregiver whenever I make mistakes with work or my husband's meds. On the worst days, I catch myself thinking it would be easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up, and I've even thought about how to make it look like an accident, which honestly scares me.

Have you ever had a stretch of at least 2 weeks where your only problem was trouble sleeping, without feeling depressed, losing interest, or having any periods of unusually high energy or needing much less sleep?

No, I’ve never had a period where sleep was the only issue. Over the past year, my sleep problems have always been closely tied to my mood—either happening alongside my deep sadness and exhaustion, or during those brief, wired phases where I felt like I didn't need sleep at all.
Have you ever had a full 2-week period where you felt depressed or lost interest in things, but had no episodes of unusually high energy, racing thoughts, or needing much less sleep?

No, because over the past year, my long periods of feeling down and losing interest have always been interrupted by those high-energy, wired phases where I barely slept. Since these cycles started about a year ago, I haven't had a long stretch of depression without also experiencing those highs.
Have you ever had a full 2-week period where the only problem was insomnia, without feeling depressed, losing interest, or having any episodes of unusually high energy or needing much less sleep?

No, I have never had a period of just isolated insomnia. My sleep issues have always been completely tied to my mood—either I'm lying awake anxious and exhausted during my deep lows, or I'm feeling so wired during my high-energy phases that I don't feel like I need sleep at all.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports bipolar I disorder with a current major depressive episode: the patient reports a near-year of persistent depressive symptoms with marked anhedonia, low mood, poor appetite, guilt/worthlessness, impaired concentration, and suicidal ideation. She also has clear past manic episodes lasting about a week with decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, increased goal-directed activity, racing/rapid thoughts, irritability, impulsive spending, and risky driving, causing occupational and social impairment. No psychosis or hospitalization was reported. The current presentation is depressive, and the available candidate code best matching bipolar depression is F31.4.
